newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila SEC task force to probe stocks plunge.
newsitem.headline: Manila SEC task force to probe stocks plunge.

text.p: The Philippine Securities and Exchange Commission has created a task force to investigate recent steep falls on the Manila bourse, the SEC's chief said on Thursday.
SEC chairman Perfecto Yasay said the commission would summon brokers who traded heavily in counters which were sold down due to negative rumours and ask them to explain their action.
"If they can't explain their positions, they're already liable ... They don't have to be caught red-handed," Yasay said.
The task force would also look at whether there was any insider trading involved.

The main index of the Philippine Stock Exchange has lost more than 16 percent since the start of April. Yasay told reporters that although no criminal charges would be filed against the brokers, administrative sanctions could be imposed.
On Wednesday, Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo ordered the SEC to use the full force of the law to rid the exchange of share manipulators.
The Philippines has no statute against rumour-mongering and a weak law against insider trading. No brokers have been arrested for insider trading.
